title: Dr. Kildare
paragraphs: Medical drama derived from MGM’s Dr. Kildare screen property and Max Brand characters.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: MGM transcribed syndication (1949 to 1951).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Lew Ayres (performer), Lionel Barrymore (performer), Walter Schumann (composer and conductor), Dick Joy (announcer), Raymond Katz (producer), Max Brand (creator), and [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]] (performer).

The stories often return to medical diagnosis, treatment and hospital care, family, relationships and patient social life, infection, disease and public health, mental health, addiction and psychological treatment, surgery, operations and trauma, and disability, paralysis and rehabilitation.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes MGM film property adapted for transcribed radio, Postwar transcribed radio syndication, Postwar popular medical drama, and Radio in the early television transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|richard-diamond-private-detective|Richard Diamond, Private Detective]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], and [[show|escape|Escape]].
